clue.text: Pudding — one of more than 100?

definitions.meaning: a suet pudding studded with currants or raisins
a Dalmatian, as in the story of the hundred and one Dalmatians

explanation.walkthrough: SPOTTED DOG is a British steamed suet pudding with currants; it is also jokey slang for a Dalmatian, and there were 101 of them in the famous story.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a currant suet pudding and, playfully, a Dalmatian, one of the hundred and one.

clue.text: Portrait by Whistler, possibly — see the butterfly

definitions.meaning: a picture of a woman, by the American artist Whistler perhaps

explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a link. Whistler painted portraits of women, and Whistler also signed his works with a butterfly emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a woman in a painting and a familiar migrant butterfly species.

clue.text: Distinctive characteristic of French observed in land and water transport

indicators.note: the French word can be observed inside the land vehicle's letters

parts.note: a tram is a land vehicle, here as land transport
de is French for of
an ark is a boat

explanation.surface: A French feature turns up in both trams and boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' serves both: TRAM for land, ARK for water.
explanation.definitionFit: A hallmark or signature feature identifying a person or thing.

clue.text: It's upheld by a man given to disputation

indicators.note: by here means within, so the man's name holds the other letters

parts.note: Eric is a man's name

indicators.note: held up in a down clue, so the letters are read bottom to top

explanation.surface: Something is supported by a man who loves to argue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upheld' turns the word upward, as a down clue is read, and 'by' here means held within the man's name rather than beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eristic describes argument for its own sake, fond of dispute.

clue.text: Converted, man had pity on sad friends in dire predicament

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A converted man took pity on sad friends in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek legend Pythias was condemned to death and his friend Damon stood hostage for him, a byword for loyal friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek legend's two loyal companions risked death for each other, a byword for friendship under threat.

clue.text: Newspaper — look over letters in the middle

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the look word sits above the next piece

parts.note: gaze means look

indicators.note: the central letters of the word letters are taken

explanation.surface: Someone looks over the letters page in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the middle' takes TTE, the centre of LETTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazette is a journal or newspaper, especially an official one.

clue.text: Class make animal's bed

definitions.meaning: a school year group or grade
the resting hollow of a hare

explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: a school class, to make, and a hare's resting place.
explanation.definitionFit: A school year is a form, to fashion is to form, and a hare lies up in its form.

clue.text: Pigment got from mineral aggregate found round church

indicators.note: the mineral word is found surrounding the church abbreviation

parts.note: ore is a mineral deposit

explanation.surface: A pigment is extracted from rock found near a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown colouring made from iron oxide.

clue.text: In summer I traversed desert

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: During the summer someone crossed a desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like the Sahara; it is the noun meaning what one deserves, as in just deserts.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserts are what one deserves, so desert means worthiness.

clue.text: Exam I entered in strange, artificial habitat

parts.note: a viva is an oral examination

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the word for strange, so it has entered it

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A student taking an exam finds the setting strange and artificial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' as British slang for odd is old-fashioned but common in crosswords; a viva is an oral exam at British universities.
explanation.definitionFit: A vivarium is an enclosure set up to house living animals in conditions copying their natural surroundings.

clue.text: Spot woman's instrument

parts.note: a zit is a pimple or spot
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A pimple appears on a woman's musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A zither is a stringed musical instrument played flat on the lap or a table.

clue.text: Avenue losing tree when it's shortened

definitions.text: Avenue losing tree when it's shortened

parts.words: Avenue losing tree when it's shortened
parts.note: a road whose name, written short, drops the four letters spelling a tree and leaves its two-letter abbreviation

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a road; remove TREE from the middle and what remains, S and T, is its usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A road in a town is a thoroughfare much like an avenue, abbreviated St.

clue.text: Staff union and I splitting payment for nourishment

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a union for school staff

indicators.note: the letter goes between letters of the payment word, splitting it apart

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for property

explanation.surface: A teachers' union demands a share of the payment for nourishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT was Britain's National Union of Teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrient is a substance that provides nourishment to a living thing.

clue.text: Chart of Iran modified to show Egypt, etc.

indicators.note: modified means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A map of Iran is changed to show Egypt and its neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is one of the countries in the northern part of the African continent.

clue.text: Plan that's well-nigh perfect

indicators.note: almost, so the word for perfect is taken short of its final letter

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: A scheme that is almost flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan or notion in the mind is a synonym for the answer.

clue.text: Artist is after artificially balanced light source

indicators.note: the artist's letters come after the rearranged ones
done artificially, so the letters are rearranged rather than natural

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, stands for an artist

explanation.surface: A painter pursues an artificially balanced source of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balanced' looks like a description of the light source, but it is the fodder that 'artificially' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A candelabra is a branched holder for several candles or lamps, a source of light.

clue.text: Heavenly limo Arabs ordered

indicators.note: ordered means arranged anew, so the letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Some Arabs ordered a heavenly limousine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the gods, so ambrosial means divine.

clue.text: Impudent fellow, a scruff, caught by sailors

indicators.note: the sailors' word holds the other letters as if they were caught

parts.note: jacks, as in jack tars, are sailors
the scruff is the nape of the neck

explanation.surface: A scruffy cheeky fellow is caught by a group of sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a scruff' looks like a scruffy person but is A + NAPE, the back of the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackanapes is a cheeky, conceited person.

clue.text: Endlessly holding up plant

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top
the word loses its final letter

parts.note: holding, as in maintaining a claim, means alleging

explanation.surface: Someone endlessly holds up a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts ALLEGING to ALLEGIN; 'up' reverses it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigella is a flowering plant, love-in-a-mist, whose seeds are used as a spice.

clue.text: Mule — one not very sure-footed?

definitions.meaning: a backless shoe for wearing indoors
someone liable to lose their footing

explanation.walkthrough: A mule looks like the animal, famously sure-footed; it is a backless shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A mule is a backless house shoe, and one who slips is unsteady on their feet.

clue.text: Primarily brass Thai circulates, not I

definitions.text: Primarily brass Thai circulates, not I

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so the opening letter of the next word is taken
letters that circulate move around and so change order
the letter named after not is left out of the word

explanation.surface: Thai money circulates as cash, says someone who does not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulates' rearranges THA (Thai with 'not I' dropping I) to AHT, after B. As a whole the clue describes Thai brass, slang for money, in circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: The baht is the currency unit of Thailand, the money that circulates there.

clue.text: Sense agreement amongst crew

indicators.note: the agreement word is set amongst the letters of the crew word

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew
yes is a word of agreement

explanation.surface: A rowing crew senses agreement among its members.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a rowing boat crew of eight oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the five senses.

clue.text: Stand as moderate Labour leader

parts.note: to ease is to moderate or lessen

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Labour

explanation.surface: A moderate stands as Labour leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' looks like a political candidacy; it is the artist's stand. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a frame standing to hold a painting.

clue.text: Finally in fable, fox, you recall, out-thought crow

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: In Aesop's fable the fox outwits the crow, as you may remember.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crow' looks like the bird in the fable; it is the verb to gloat.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast or rejoice triumphantly.

clue.text: Batting with cricket side, son makes poor shots

parts.note: a batter is in, at the crease
the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A son batting for a cricket team plays poor shots.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the off side is the half of the field the batter faces. An in-off in billiards or snooker is a shot where the cue ball goes into a pocket off another ball, a foul.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards these are shots where the cue ball drops in a pocket after hitting another ball, giving away points.

clue.text: Sudden outburst of temper can make you cry

definitions.meaning: a brief violent gust or flare-up, of wind or of anger
to scream or bawl noisily, as a baby does

explanation.walkthrough: 'can make you' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sudden gust or flare-up and to bawl loudly like an infant.

clue.text: Understood I elected representative in accordance with law

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
licit means lawful

explanation.surface: It is taken as read that a member of parliament acts within the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is implied without being stated, tacitly understood.

clue.text: Departed after a delay

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes both someone recently dead and something arriving behind time.

clue.text: A litre consumed by European from Newcastle or Perth, perhaps

indicators.note: the European word swallows the other letters, holding them within

parts.note: an Austrian is a European

explanation.surface: A European drinks a litre of beer in a northern English or Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Newcastle and Perth look like places in England and Scotland; both are also cities in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcastle and Perth are cities in Australia, so someone from there is of that country.
